methodology: Every case-law judgment was made by reading the actual chunk's own headnote text (and, for CL1, the embedded case name 'Khurshid Bibi v. Muhammad Amin') directly from var/rag/caselaw_chunked/*.json -- not inferred from the query. Constitution judgments reuse the article/chunk mapping already verified by direct source reading in evaluation/results/phase2a_constitution_audit.json (Phase 2A of this project), now extended to a single primary representative chunk per query rather than the whole article -- explicitly marked incomplete/representative, not exhaustive, since several of these articles (e.g. 175A, 199) have many clauses beyond the one chosen chunk.

judgments.rationale: Headnote directly states the standard: wife entitled to khula as of right if she satisfies the court's conscience that living together would otherwise force her into a hateful union. Cites the landmark case Khurshid Bibi v. Muhammad Amin.

CL1.completeness: representative, not exhaustive -- other cases almost certainly restate or refine this standard; only this one verified instance is used.

judgments.rationale: Headnote states the Family Courts Act does not define 'maintenance' and that courts apply its dictionary meaning (financial support, typically after separation/divorce).

Headnote directly rules that Qanun-e-Shahadat, 1984 and the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 do NOT apply to proving a dowry-articles claim under Family Courts Act s.17(1) -- directly on-point evidentiary ruling.
Headnote directly states: High Court in constitutional jurisdiction could not pre-empt the Guardian Judge's jurisdiction (Guardians and Wards Act ss.12 & 25, Constitution Art.199).
Headnote directly states: where parties did not mutually agree to khula, the court could still allow it in consideration of the wife giving up her unpaid dower.
Headnote directly states: no fixed yardstick for the factum of hatred; inferred from circumstances, especially the wife's own statement to the court.
Clause (1) enumerates the High Court's writ-jurisdiction powers directly.
